source.title: Toy Combinatorial Interpretability Models Reveal Lottery Tickets in Early Feature Space

record.tranche_reason: The study measures feature-code placement and row-level competition in a clause-structured toy network, using a different method from the original superposition model.
record.gate_note: Rows below cover the paper's own results on crowded-row rejection, survival of code precursors, and code-family relocation. The ticket-accuracy benchmarks do not directly measure the claim's feature geometry or competition, so they are not rows. The discussion of Toy Models of Superposition and other cited results is not counted as new evidence.
record.test_reason: This is a lottery-ticket study in a clause-structured DNF toy model. It uses superposition (Elhage et al.) as an interpretive lens for row-level competition among code locations during dense SGD. It never measures what any version names: no sparsity-dependent phase change, no near-orthogonal geometry, no importance-based allocation, no polysemanticity cause, no LLM or SAE results. The closest result, rejection rising with row load (Fig. 5), concerns which candidate ticket locations survive training. It is a related construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V1 or V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that, in this toy DNF model, winning lottery tickets are support-induced feature-space scaffolds: families of code precursors near final codes at initialization. Dense SGD sharpens some precursors and rejects others on crowded rows ('under superposition pressure'), and sparse retraining can re-express a family on another row. They limit the claim to a discrete model organism.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a clause-structured DNF network and combinatorial code-distance, margin, and row-load diagnostics; it does not reproduce the original superposition model or its sparsity/geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported rejection probability increases with row near-load. The paper also reports family-level recovery across multiple embedding and clause-count settings, but the result described here does not give setting-specific values.

fits_no_version.finding: In dense SGD of a toy DNF network, initially plausible oracle-supported code locations are rejected more often on rows carrying more near-codes. Rejection probability rises with row near-load (Fig. 5, qualitative). The authors read this as competition under superposition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During training, candidate feature codes competing for the same hidden neuron are pruned more often on crowded neurons (load-dependent code selection).

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse retraining recovers the same clause/template code family on a different row more often than on the same row (Fig. 3, Fig. 17), so the row carrier is interchangeable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature codes in superposed toy networks are identified at family level, not by a fixed carrier neuron.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed W1 budget of 256, random sparse expansion to 32 rows raises aligned code count from 46.3 to 97.8 over a 16-row dense layer (Table 1). More row carriers allow more codes. The authors present this as confirming prior work (Kong et al. 2025).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding row carriers at fixed parameter count increases the number of feature codes a toy network represents.

record.problems: The evidence is limited to a discrete toy DNF setting and does not measure activation co-occurrence sparsity, near-orthogonality, angular geometry, or feature importance. The relevant figure results are described qualitatively without numerical values or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Ticket benchmark results in Tables 1–4 and the detector sweeps were not extracted as rows because they primarily measure accuracy, code counts, or mask-selection performance rather than the claim's overlap geometry or row-level competition.

untested.parts: Sparsity-dependent transition, nearly orthogonal directions, regular geometry: none measured.
Whether neurons are polysemantic because of capacity pressure, and whether important features get dedicated dimensions: not measured.
Polysemanticity without capacity pressure: not tested.
SAE feature completeness, stability or canonicity: not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1/V2 'supports' labels are not justified. Superposition is invoked interpretively; the measured quantities are lottery-ticket dynamics. Original source not involved. Ticket benchmark tables (accuracy, code recall, Jaccard) bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test a sparsity-dependent transition, feature co-activation sparsity, near-orthogonal directions, or regular angular geometry.
It measures competition and sharing among clause-code carriers, but not feature importance or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while less important features share them.
It does not test polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
It does not measure feature distributions or dictionary recovery in LLMs.
It does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
It does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.check: Rejection probability vs row near-load measures survival of oracle-supported candidate code locations during dense training. It does not measure overlapping near-orthogonal feature directions (V1) or whether polysemanticity arises from capacity limits with importance-based allocation (V2). The value is figure-only with no numbers.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: row-level code competition in the clause-structured DNF toy model
reader_labels.reason: Rejection increases with row near-load, and code families can be recovered on different carrier rows, consistent with overlap and interference in this tested setting (R1, R3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: candidate code carriers during dense training and family recovery after sparse retraining
reader_labels.reason: More crowded rows reject more plausible candidates, while family recovery exceeds same-site recovery, supporting a limited-capacity competition account for carrier sharing in this toy model (R1, R3).
